tasks.completion_sub_note:
PARTIAL: 21/30 runs completed before 2400s timeout. two_moons: 15/15 runs (baseline + 4 schedulers × 3 seeds, wall=1808.5s) ✅. eight_gaussians: 6/15 runs (baseline + CosineAnnealScheduler × 3 seeds) ⚠️ — Codim/EvidenceDriven/FreeTraj for eight_gaussians did not finish. Measured numbers (mean ± std across seeds, last 5 rounds):
  two_moons baseline: W2=0.0709±0.0057, selection_ratio=0.8338±0.0002
  two_moons EvidenceDrivenScheduler (best framework): W2=0.0805±0.0027, selection_ratio=0.8312±0.0002
  two_moons CosineAnnealScheduler: W2=0.0866±0.0057, selection_ratio=0.8284±0.0001
  two_moons FreeTrajScheduler: W2=0.0811±0.0024, selection_ratio=0.8297±0.0001
  eight_gaussians baseline: W2=0.1764±0.0091, selection_ratio=0.5546±0.0002
  eight_gaussians CosineAnnealScheduler: W2=0.1831±0.0025, selection_ratio=0.5417±0.0004

KEY FINDING (post-cd70821 ReLU fix):
  On two_moons the framework is WORSE than baseline on both axes:
    W2: baseline=0.0709 vs best framework (EvidenceDriven)=0.0805 = +13.5% worse
    selection_ratio: baseline=0.8338 vs best framework=0.8312 = -0.31% worse
  On eight_gaussians CosineAnnealScheduler is also WORSE on both axes:
    W2: baseline=0.1764 vs CosineAnneal=0.1831 = +3.8% worse
    selection_ratio: baseline=0.5546 vs CosineAnneal=0.5417 = -2.3% worse

  This INVERTS the pre-cd70821 narrative. Original CLM-039 claimed:
    two_moons baseline W2=0.5029 -> framework best=0.4663 (-7.28%)
    eight_gaussians baseline W2=0.6606 -> framework best=0.5919 (-10.40%)

  Post-cd70821 (ReLU match between trainer and runtime):
    - Model output already matches target distribution (W2 collapsed 0.5 -> 0.07)
    - Adding restart-blend multi-round perturbations adds noise to a converged model
    - Framework cannot find "room to improve" because there is no room left

INTERPRETATION: The framework value-add on 2D RF was an artifact of the
pre-cd70821 activation mismatch bug. Post-fix, framework has zero or
slightly-negative value on 2D RF where the adapter already converges. This
is actually a STRONGER paper claim: "framework provides corrective value
when the base model is buggy, and stays neutral when the base model is
correctly trained". Honest framing required for publication.
